# gh-2372: [daily-publish] stale release drafts swept

## Description

**Sweep run:** https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/45117164332
**Swept:** 1 stale pipeline-created draft(s) older than 24h
- `v1.0.760` — created 2026-11-21T05:29:27Z by @IstiN; creating run: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/44870476733

**Fresh drafts (<24h):** 1 — untouched (an in-flight run may own them)

A stale draft means a `gh release create` step died between asset upload and publish — check the creating run's failed step. Recurrence means a lifecycle guard is missing (issue #282).

---
Auto-filed by the daily draft sweeper; auto-closes when a sweep finds nothing stale.

## Machine jobs
- [x] ▶ dev (fa-bug-dev) · [run](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/45117908769) · started 05:29 · done 06:08 ✅

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 2373
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/2373
- **Title**: gh-2372 [daily-publish] stale release drafts swept
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-2372` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 7
- **Additions**: +923
- **Deletions**: -7
- **Created**: 2026-11-23T06:07:53Z
- **Updated**: 2026-11-23T06:09:40Z

## PR Description

Closes #2372
### Root Cause

The daily sweep filed gh-2372 for draft `v1.0.760` — but the release itself was published by a green train; nothing died. Inside one `build-macos.yml` run the sibling jobs (`build-macos-cli-arm64/x64`, `build-extension`) race `release_lazy_draft.sh` for the same tag; when their view→create calls interleave, **both `gh release create --draft` calls succeed** (GitHub does not enforce one release per tag for drafts) and a twin draft is born. The train publishes exactly one; the twin rots 24h+ until the sweeper deletes it and re-files the recurring issue. Evidence: v1.0.760's published object (453463937, marker `run/44870476733/job/build-extension`) and the swept twin share `created_at 2026-11-21T05:29:27Z` and the same run; v1.0.763's twin (454339915, zero assets, marker `run/45007933749/job/build-extension`) was still live when the sweep counted it "fresh: 1". No guard covered it: the failure-path guards never fire (all jobs green) and `release_draft_dedupe.sh` matches only the **train's** own-run twins — child-run twins were invisible.

### Fix

- `scripts/release_draft_twin_dedupe.sh` (new) — after a successful draft create, the creator self-deletes its OWN draft (exact `release-draft-owner` marker match, delete by id) when an older (lower id) same-tag release exists that is published or pipeline-created; the caller then attaches into the winner by tag. Deterministic election (ids are monotonic), best-effort (warn + green; the sweeper stays the backstop), human drafts never win and are never touched (E1).
- `scripts/release_lazy_draft.sh`, `scripts/release_attach_or_create.sh` — call the dedupe right after their successful creates.
- `scripts/sweep_stale_drafts.sh` — a MARKED draft whose tag already carries a published release is reclaimed immediately (fresh **or** stale) as routine hygiene (gh-236 convention: own summary/issue section, never a finding, so a residual twin can't re-file the recurring issue); the clean-sweep auto-close names twin reclaims. The misleading "a `gh release create` step died" prose can no longer fire for this shape.

### Test Coverage

- `test/release_draft_twin_dedupe_test.dart` (new, 9 tests): lazy-draft loser self-deletes its twin; winner keeps; human draft never wins/is never deleted; published-older wins; delete-blip stays green; attach-or-create path; no-op when our draft is gone; malformed identity fails loud; wiring order in both creators.
- `test/release_fresh_twin_reclaim_test.dart` (new, 5 tests): fresh/stale marked twins on a published tag reclaimed as hygiene with no issue filed; auto-close names reclaims; unpublished-tag fresh drafts untouched; unmarked author-bot drafts keep the bot-bucket finding.
- Full suite: `dart test --exclude-tags integration` — **14872 passed, 16 skipped** (environment-conditional skips); the release family (202 pre-existing + 14 new) re-run green on the final tree.
- `dart analyze` — 0 issues in touched files (repo's pre-existing 78 unrelated issues unchanged from base).

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Post-create twin-draft self-dedupe (gh-2372) — the success-path half of
+# the issue #282 invariant for CHILD-run drafts.
+#
+# Why this exists: the view→create race between sibling jobs of ONE
+# release run is NOT benign for DRAFT objects. GitHub does not enforce
+# one release per tag for drafts (gh-1899, v1.0.641: twin drafts 87 ms
+# apart), so when two legs of the same build-macos.yml run hit the race
+# window — production: the SAME SECOND (v1.0.760: build-extension won +
+# was published, its build-macos-cli twin rotted 43h and was swept by
+# gh-2372; v1.0.763: build-macos-cli-arm64 won, the build-extension twin
+# is a live zero-asset draft) — BOTH `gh release create --draft` calls
+# succeed and two twin drafts are born. The tag train publishes exactly
+# ONE object; the twin rots until the daily sweeper deletes it and
+# re-files the recurring "[daily-publish] stale release drafts swept"
+# issue. No existing guard fires: every creating job SUCCEEDED (the
+# failure-path guards never run), and release_draft_dedupe.sh matches
+# only twins stamped with the TRAIN's GITHUB_RUN_ID — child-run twins
+# carry the build-macos run's id and are invisible to it.
+#
+# This closes the race at the source. Call it RIGHT AFTER a successful
+# draft create (release_lazy_draft.sh + release_attach_or_create.sh):
+#
+#   - OUR draft = a same-tag DRAFT whose body carries EXACTLY this job's
+#     ownership marker (release-draft-owner: run/<id>/job/<name>, the
+#     stampers' exact shape; capture + full-value equality, so run/111
+#     can never match run/1111 — the release_draft_guard.sh discipline).
+#     A job can only ever delete the draft(s) it just created.
+#   - WINNER ELECTION (deterministic): the OLDEST same-tag release wins —
+#     ids are monotonic, so the first-created object always has the
+#     lowest id and a later creator always sees it in its listing; no
+#     interleaving can make both jobs keep a twin. The winner is any
+#     older same-tag release that is PUBLISHED (the train already flipped
+#     the sibling) or PIPELINE-created: a well-formed
+#     release-draft-owner marker in the body, author.type == Bot, a
+#     *[bot] login, or the machine account (DAILY_PUBLISH_ASSIGNEE —
+#     the sweeper's exact gh-2287 bucket rule, kept consistent).
+#   - When a winner exists, every draft carrying OUR exact marker is
+#     deleted BY ID via the API — never a tag-based delete (drafts may
+#     carry an empty tag_name; under duplicate releases a tag lookup is
+#     ambiguous — the very class this guards). The caller then attaches
+#     into the winner by tag — release_lazy_draft's gh-1801 contract
+#     "the loser just uploads into the winner's release", now actually
+#     true.
+#   - HUMAN drafts (unmarked, User author) never win and never trigger a
+#     self-delete (E1): the pipeline must not ride a human draft, and a
+#     human draft must never be deleted by automation. Our draft stays
+#     and is reclaimed by the 24h sweeper as today.
+#   - BEST-EFFORT (gh-1899 review convention): every failure here — the
+#     listing blips, one failed DELETE — warns and exits 0. The call
+#     site is a green create path; a cleanup blip must never red a leg
+#     whose leftover is harmless (the sweeper remains the backstop, and
+#     sweep_stale_drafts.sh reclaims fresh twins whose tag is already
+#     published). Only a malformed RELEASE_DRAFT_IDENTITY fails loud —
+#     the marker-stamping scripts already validate it pre-create; a
+#     marker nothing could ever match is a configuration bug, not a
+#     cleanup blip.
+#
+# Usage: release_draft_twin_dedupe.sh <tag>
+# Env: GITHUB_REPOSITORY, GITHUB_RUN_ID, GITHUB_JOB (Actions defaults),
+#      RELEASE_DRAFT_IDENTITY (optional leg-suffixed override, same as
+#      release_lazy_draft.sh / release_draft_guard.sh),
+#      DAILY_PUBLISH_ASSIGNEE (default ai-teammate), GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN.
+set -euo pipefail
+
+tag="${1:?usage: release_draft_twin_dedupe.sh <tag>}"
+repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:?GITHUB_REPOSITORY must be set}"
+identity="${RELEASE_DRAFT_IDENTITY:-run/${GITHUB_RUN_ID:?GITHUB_RUN_ID must be set (GitHub Actions default env)}/job/${GITHUB_JOB:?GITHUB_JOB must be set (GitHub Actions default env)}}"
+assignee="${DAILY_PUBLISH_ASSIGNEE:-ai-teammate}"
+
+printf '%s' "$identity" | grep -Eq '^run/[0-9]+/job/[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$' || {
+  echo "::error::RELEASE_DRAFT_IDENTITY '$identity' does not match 'run/<id>/job/<name>' — the marker we stamped could never be matched by any guard" >&2
+  exit 1
+}
+
+# One paginated listing answers both questions (ours + winner). A blip
+# degrades to keep — never judge twins off a partial roster.
+list=$(gh api --paginate "repos/$repo/releases" 2>/dev/null) || {
+  echo "::warning::release twin dedupe: the release listing failed — cannot judge twins, keeping our draft for $tag" >&2
+  exit 0
+}
+
+# Same-tag drafts carrying EXACTLY our marker (capture + full-value
+# equality — the prefix trap release_draft_guard.sh pins: run/111/job/x
+# must never match run/1111/job/x or run/111/job/x-longer).
+mine_ids=$(printf '%s' "$list" | jq -s -r --arg tag "$tag" --arg id "$identity" '
+  [ flatten[]
+    | select(.draft == true and .tag_name == $tag)
+    | select((((.body // "")
+        | (capture("release-draft-owner: (?<m>run/[0-9]+/job/[A-Za-z0-9_-]+)")? | .m) // "")
+        == $id))
+    | .id | tostring ]
+  | unique | .[]')
+
+if [ -z "$mine_ids" ]; then
+  echo "release twin dedupe: no own draft for $tag in the listing — nothing to clean"
+  exit 0
+fi
+
+# Deterministic winner: any older (lower id — first-created) same-tag
+# release that is published or pipeline-created.
+mine_min=$(printf '%s\n' "$mine_ids" | sort -n | head -1)
+winner=$(printf '%s' "$list" | jq -s -r --arg tag "$tag" --arg assignee "$assignee" --argjson mine "$mine_min" '
+  [ flatten[]
+    | select(.tag_name == $tag and .id < $mine)
+    | select(.draft == false
+        or ((.author.type // "User") == "Bot")
+        or ((.author.login // "") | test("\\[bot\\]$"))
+        or ((.author.login // "") == $assignee)
+        or ((.body // "") | test("release-draft-owner: run/[0-9]+/job/[A-Za-z0-9_-]+"))) ]
+  | length > 0')
+
+if [ "$winner" != "true" ]; then
+  echo "release twin dedupe: our draft for $tag is the oldest same-tag release — it stays"
+  exit 0
+fi
+
+deleted=0
+while IFS= read -r id; do
+  [ -n "$id" ] || continue
+  if gh api -X DELETE "repos/$repo/releases/$id" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    deleted=$((deleted + 1))
+  else
+    echo "::warning::release twin dedupe: deleting our twin draft $id for $tag failed — the daily sweeper reclaims it (fresh twins whose tag is published are reclaimed immediately; gh-2372)" >&2
+  fi
+done <<< "$mine_ids"
+
+if [ "$deleted" -gt 0 ]; then
+  echo "::warning::release twin dedupe: deleted $deleted own twin draft(s) for $tag — an older release already owns the tag (the same-run sibling create race, gh-2372); the caller attaches into the winner by tag (gh-1801 tolerance), nothing was lost: the twin carried only our unpublished assets" >&2
+fi
+exit 0

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. This file is
the agent ENTRY document: the harness merges it into the system prompt with
a ~19 KB entry budget, so it must stay small enough to be fully visible.
Ceiling: **≤ 300 lines / ≤ 20 KB** — enforced by
`scripts/check_agents_md_size.sh` (pre-commit hook via `ci_fast_gate.sh` +
the CI `static` job). Subsystem essays live in `docs/` — index:
`docs/README.md`. Keep entries factual: paths, commands, invariants.

## Module map

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph CORE["SDK - flutter_agent_harness, pure Dart (lib/)"]
        AI["ai: providers, agent loop, sessions, compaction"]
        TOLS["tools: approval, redact, hashline, memory"]
        HOSTS["hosts: shared wiring, messaging, a2a, hub"]
    end
    subgraph PKG["packages/ - sibling Dart packages"]
        FAUI["fa_ui: widgets incl. trajectory"]
        DAP["dap_hub, fa_llm, fa_llm_mock"]
    end
    CLI["fa CLI - bin/ + lib/src/cli: TUI, slash commands, headless"]
    APP["Flutter app - flutter_app/: desktop, mobile, web shells"]
    EXT["Browser extension - browser_ext/ + lib/src/browser + serve_bridge"]
    OFFICE["Office add-in - office_addin/ + FA_HOST=office host"]
    GOLDEN["UI golden & styles - golden tests, themes, ui tests"]
    NETW["fa_network - external Go backend + network clients"]
    CORE --> CLI
    CORE --> APP
    CORE --> EXT
    PKG --> APP
    PKG --> CLI
    APP --> OFFICE
    CLI --> NETW
    APP --> NETW
    EXT --> NETW
    GOLDEN --> APP
    GOLDEN --> FAUI
```

## Project layout — one line per subsystem

Full subsystem reference: `docs/agents/sdk-subsystems.md` (SDK) +
`docs/agents/flutter-app-subsystems.md` (app/packages/repo-level).

**SDK core (`lib/`, pure Dart):**

- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers, session modes, per-tool overrides, critical-bash interceptor, per-turn grants.
- `lib/src/tools/` — `ask`/`request_secret`/media tools, `read` selectors + archives + sqlite, background shell jobs, availability + load modes.
- `lib/src/env/` — `ExecutionEnv` impls: `LocalShell` (setsid, killTree, drain caps, self-signal immunity), session-correlation vars, in-memory default.
- `lib/src/agent/` — FinalizeGate, tool pairing, session image registry.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — trajectory ledger core; goldens under `test/trajectory/goldens/`.
- `lib/src/redact/` — layered secret redaction (prompt, tool args, output, logs).
- `lib/src/hashline/` — `[path#TAG]` patch language (SWAP/DEL/INS, stale-tag rejection).
- `lib/src/compaction/` — branch summarization + AutoCompactor → policy: `docs/compaction.md`.
- `lib/src/lsp/`, `lib/src/mcp/` — `lsp` + MCP protocol tooling (lazy servers, pure-Dart transports).
- `lib/src/model_roles/` — roles/fallbacks/keyring/watchdogs + provider catalog; `lib/src/ttsr/` — streaming-interrupt rules.
- `lib/src/skills/`, `lib/src/prompts/` — skills discovery; AGENTS/CLAUDE/GOAL/DESIGN auto-merge into the system prompt.
- `lib/src/task/`, `lib/src/messaging/`, `lib/src/session/attach/` — subagents, inbox fabric, attached sessions → `docs/subagents/README.md`.
- `lib/src/memory/` — long-term memory (hosted `flutter_agent_memory` package) → pitfalls: `docs/memory-churn.md`.
- `lib/src/a2a/` — Agent2Agent client/server/manager (`fa serve --a2a`).
- `bin/fah.dart` + `lib/src/cli/` — the `fa` CLI: REPL, slash commands, headless/serve modes → `docs/agents/cli.md`.
- `lib/src/cube/` — fa_cube sandbox profiles → `docs/cubes.md`; `lib/src/cli/hep.dart` — HEP event protocol → `docs/hep.md`.
- `lib/src/web_search/` — `web_search` (DDG keyless → keyed providers); `tool/fa-clip/` — native macOS pasteboard helper.

**packages/ + app shells:**

- `packages/fa_ui/` — reusable widgets (incl. trajectory) → `docs/agents/fa-ui.md`; `dap_hub`, `fa_llm`, `fa_llm_mock` → `docs/dap.md`.
- `flutter_app/` — the Flutter app (desktop/mobile/web) → `docs/agents/flutter-app.md`; services one-liner: `docs/agents/services.md`; JS apps: `docs/agents/js-apps.md`; HomeKit/Calendar/CodeMie: `docs/agents/system-integrations.md`.
- `browser_ext/` + `lib/src/browser/` + `bin/serve_bridge.dart` — browser extension + WebSocket bridge → `docs/browser-extension.md`.
- `office_addin/` + FA_HOST=office app host — Office add-in → `docs/outlook-addin.md`.
- `fa_network` — external Go backend bridged via the DAP hub (channel-id caveats: `docs/dap.md` §14).
- `site/`, `scripts/`, `docs/subagents/` — landing page (privacy sync), gates + codegen, subagents master plan → `docs/agents/flutter-app-subsystems.md`.

## Hard architecture rules (stay inline)

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.
- Barrel `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart`: grouped **APPEND-ONLY** export
  sections — one `// ── <subsystem> ──` header per group, sorted by path
  within a group, new exports append to their group. No mini-barrels, no
  re-sorting (gh-1232).
- God-file ceiling: no `.dart` file over **2800** lines (crap4dart `loc`
  gate). Target < 2000 for primary files; split by concern into `part`
  files — never by extracting public API.

## Working in parallel (shared checkout + worktrees)

Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked; run no
heavy commands (full suites/analyze) in it; never `git stash` the user's
WIP; talk to peer agents through the messaging fabric, not their files.
Worktrees only if genuinely required — ask first, create detached under
`.worktrees/<name>/` from the remote tracking ref, remove when done.
Full policy: `docs/agents/parallel-worktrees.md`.

## Memory (footnote)

Before any non-trivial task, **search memory first** (`memory_search`,
then `memory_list` for fuzzy topics). Scopes: **project** = this repo
(`.fah/memory/note/` since gh-2185 — local-only, not committed; the
user's files: read freely, write only via `memory_add`), **user** = global/private. `memory_add` stores durable facts
only; supersede by delete + add — never leave solved problems to rot. The
host recomposes the `<memory>` prompt section after every add; tool wiring
is `memoryTools` + `lib/src/memory/`. Churn pitfalls: `docs/memory-churn.md`;
usage details: `docs/agents/memory-usage.md`.

## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done: coverage first (`test/goldens/` + `golden_guard_test.dart`
map), real fonts (`ensureGoldenFonts`), full frames (1280x800 / 390x844),
determinism, eyes on pixels after `--update-goldens`, green
`flutter test test/goldens` + `scripts/check_goldens.py` (orphan snapshots
hard-fail). Full rules: `docs/agents/golden-tests.md`.

## Prompts live outside Dart code

Every LLM prompt is a Markdown file under `prompts/**` (YAML frontmatter,
`{{token}}` placeholders) — never string literals in `.dart`. After
editing: `dart run scripts/gen_prompts.dart` regenerates the `.g.dart`
files (`test/prompts/prompts_sync_test.dart` gates drift); Codex catalog
refresh: `dart run scripts/sync_codex_models.dart`. Details:
`docs/agents/prompts.md`.

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

The hook is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI classifies
PRs through the same script (`--dry-run`) — one classifier, one threshold
set, hook/CI parity via `GATE_STAGE` markers. Path rules: docs/markdown/
prompts-only → size + analyze; lib/bin/test/pubspec → +tests, coverage,
CRAP, dup, dupx; `test/integration/**` → +integration-mock;
flutter_app/packages → +flutter; scripts/.github → everything. Invariants:

- analyze + format clean; `dart test` green — **deterministic-only**
  (mock LLM; live models never in the gate; `llm`-tagged files run only in
  the tag-only provider smoke + nightly).
- Line coverage of `lib/` ≥ 80%; jscpd < 1% core / < 3.7% app; cross-module
  dup < 0.31%; CRAP ratchet: core 12.0, app 30.0 (thresholds only-down);
  ≤ 2800 lines per `.dart` file; AGENTS.md ceiling (top of this file).
- Red-in-≥2-distinct-SHA-runs flakes quarantine via
  `scripts/test_quarantine.json`; nightly keeps running quarantined files.

Full gate text: `docs/agents/quality-gates.md`; CI workflows: `docs/ci.md`.

## Cross-platform parity

Every shared setting and interactive prompt type exists on BOTH the CLI
and the Flutter app unless fundamentally impossible — then it MUST be in
`cliOnlySettings`/`appOnlySettings` (`lib/src/parity/settings_registry.dart`)
with the reason; run `dart test test/parity/`. Host capabilities (issue
#1079): every host-wiring capability declares its 7-host matrix state AT
BIRTH (`on` / `off(reason)` / `transport`) via `wireAgentCore` — `off` is
invisible everywhere; extensions are declared surface, SDK invariants have
no override point. Full rules: `docs/agents/cross-platform-parity.md`.

## Commits and releases

- Commit as `ai.teammate <agent.ai.native@gmail.com>` (set repo-locally);
  subjects `type(scope): ...`. Release-path automation MUST use the
  fa-release-bot GitHub App token — never a PAT or `GITHUB_TOKEN`.
- Every push to main cuts an annotated tag (`scripts/auto_release.sh`);
  the tag is the single version source (pubspecs stay `0.0.0-dev`);
  releases go DRAFT-first and publish at `release-provenance` only with
  signed SHA256SUMS attached. CHANGELOG.md is curated-only (`## Unreleased`).
- `packages/fa_llm` publishes per `fa_llm-v*` tag (first publish of a new
  package is manual); every lockfile is committed and enforced
  (`scripts/check_lockfiles.sh`); TestFlight external-group + store
  pipelines have required repo variables.

Full text: `docs/agents/commits-releases.md`.

## Bench

Bench knobs (agent timeouts, stall/watch, `FA_CONN_DEBUG`, hang replay,
report semantics) → `docs/bench.md` (round-3 knobs: issue #1392).

## Docs index

`docs/README.md` indexes every canonical doc (agents/, memory-churn,
compaction, dap, cubes, redaction, hep, ci, bench, browser-extension,
outlook-addin, …). New docs must be listed there.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Post-create twin-draft self-dedupe (gh-2372) — the success-path half of
# the issue #282 invariant for CHILD-run drafts.
#
# Why this exists: the view→create race between sibling jobs of ONE
# release run is NOT benign for DRAFT objects. GitHub does not enforce
# one release per tag for drafts (gh-1899, v1.0.641: twin drafts 87 ms
# apart), so when two legs of the same build-macos.yml run hit the race
# window — production: the SAME SECOND (v1.0.760: build-extension won +
# was published, its build-macos-cli twin rotted 43h and was swept by
# gh-2372; v1.0.763: build-macos-cli-arm64 won, the build-extension twin
# is a live zero-asset draft) — BOTH `gh release create --draft` calls
# succeed and two twin drafts are born. The tag train publishes exactly
# ONE object; the twin rots until the daily sweeper deletes it and
# re-files the recurring "[daily-publish] stale release drafts swept"
# issue. No existing guard fires: every creating job SUCCEEDED (the
# failure-path guards never run), and release_draft_dedupe.sh matches
# only twins stamped with the TRAIN's GITHUB_RUN_ID — child-run twins
# carry the build-macos run's id and are invisible to it.
#
# This closes the race at the source. Call it RIGHT AFTER a successful
# draft create (release_lazy_draft.sh + release_attach_or_create.sh):
#
#   - OUR draft = a same-tag DRAFT whose body carries EXACTLY this job's
#     ownership marker (release-draft-owner: run/<id>/job/<name>, the
#     stampers' exact shape; capture + full-value equality, so run/111
#     can never match run/1111 — the release_draft_guard.sh discipline).
#     A job can only ever delete the draft(s) it just created.
#   - WINNER ELECTION (deterministic): the OLDEST same-tag release wins —
#     ids are monotonic, so the first-created object always has the
#     lowest id and a later creator always sees it in its listing; no
#     interleaving can make both jobs keep a twin. The winner is any
#     older same-tag release that is PUBLISHED (the train already flipped
#     the sibling) or PIPELINE-created: a well-formed
#     release-draft-owner marker in the body, author.type == Bot, a
#     *[bot] login, or the machine account (DAILY_PUBLISH_ASSIGNEE —
#     the sweeper's exact gh-2287 bucket rule, kept consistent).
#   - When a winner exists, every draft carrying OUR exact marker is
#     deleted BY ID via the API — never a tag-based delete (drafts may
#     carry an empty tag_name; under duplicate releases a tag lookup is
#     ambiguous — the very class this guards). The caller then attaches
#     into the winner by tag — release_lazy_draft's gh-1801 contract
#     "the loser just uploads into the winner's release", now actually
#     true.
#   - HUMAN drafts (unmarked, User author) never win and never trigger a
#     self-delete (E1): the pipeline must not ride a human draft, and a
#     human draft must never be deleted by automation. Our draft stays
#     and is reclaimed by the 24h sweeper as today.
#   - BEST-EFFORT (gh-1899 review convention): every failure here — the
#     listing blips, one failed DELETE — warns and exits 0. The call
#     site is a green create path; a cleanup blip must never red a leg
#     whose leftover is harmless (the sweeper remains the backstop, and
#     sweep_stale_drafts.sh reclaims fresh twins whose tag is already
#     published). Only a malformed RELEASE_DRAFT_IDENTITY fails loud —
#     the marker-stamping scripts already validate it pre-create; a
#     marker nothing could ever match is a configuration bug, not a
#     cleanup blip.
#
# Usage: release_draft_twin_dedupe.sh <tag>
# Env: GITHUB_REPOSITORY, GITHUB_RUN_ID, GITHUB_JOB (Actions defaults),
#      RELEASE_DRAFT_IDENTITY (optional leg-suffixed override, same as
#      release_lazy_draft.sh / release_draft_guard.sh),
#      DAILY_PUBLISH_ASSIGNEE (default ai-teammate), GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN.
set -euo pipefail

tag="${1:?usage: release_draft_twin_dedupe.sh <tag>}"
repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:?GITHUB_REPOSITORY must be set}"
identity="${RELEASE_DRAFT_IDENTITY:-run/${GITHUB_RUN_ID:?GITHUB_RUN_ID must be set (GitHub Actions default env)}/job/${GITHUB_JOB:?GITHUB_JOB must be set (GitHub Actions default env)}}"
assignee="${DAILY_PUBLISH_ASSIGNEE:-ai-teammate}"

printf '%s' "$identity" | grep -Eq '^run/[0-9]+/job/[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$' || {
  echo "::error::RELEASE_DRAFT_IDENTITY '$identity' does not match 'run/<id>/job/<name>' — the marker we stamped could never be matched by any guard" >&2
  exit 1
}

# One paginated listing answers both questions (ours + winner). A blip
# degrades to keep — never judge twins off a partial roster.
list=$(gh api --paginate "repos/$repo/releases" 2>/dev/null) || {
  echo "::warning::release twin dedupe: the release listing failed — cannot judge twins, keeping our draft for $tag" >&2
  exit 0
}

# Same-tag drafts carrying EXACTLY our marker (capture + full-value
# equality — the prefix trap release_draft_guard.sh pins: run/111/job/x
# must never match run/1111/job/x or run/111/job/x-longer).
mine_ids=$(printf '%s' "$list" | jq -s -r --arg tag "$tag" --arg id "$identity" '
  [ flatten[]
    | select(.draft == true and .tag_name == $tag)
    | select((((.body // "")
        | (capture("release-draft-owner: (?<m>run/[0-9]+/job/[A-Za-z0-9_-]+)")? | .m) // "")
        == $id))
    | .id | tostring ]
  | unique | .[]')

if [ -z "$mine_ids" ]; then
  echo "release twin dedupe: no own draft for $tag in the listing — nothing to clean"
  exit 0
fi

# Deterministic winner: any older (lower id — first-created) same-tag
# release that is published or pipeline-created.
mine_min=$(printf '%s\n' "$mine_ids" | sort -n | head -1)
winner=$(printf '%s' "$list" | jq -s -r --arg tag "$tag" --arg assignee "$assignee" --argjson mine "$mine_min" '
  [ flatten[]
    | select(.tag_name == $tag and .id < $mine)
    | select(.draft == false
        or ((.author.type // "User") == "Bot")
        or ((.author.login // "") | test("\\[bot\\]$"))
        or ((.author.login // "") == $assignee)
        or ((.body // "") | test("release-draft-owner: run/[0-9]+/job/[A-Za-z0-9_-]+"))) ]
  | length > 0')

if [ "$winner" != "true" ]; then
  echo "release twin dedupe: our draft for $tag is the oldest same-tag release — it stays"
  exit 0
fi

deleted=0
while IFS= read -r id; do
  [ -n "$id" ] || continue
  if gh api -X DELETE "repos/$repo/releases/$id" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    deleted=$((deleted + 1))
  else
    echo "::warning::release twin dedupe: deleting our twin draft $id for $tag failed — the daily sweeper reclaims it (fresh twins whose tag is published are reclaimed immediately; gh-2372)" >&2
  fi
done <<< "$mine_ids"

if [ "$deleted" -gt 0 ]; then
  echo "::warning::release twin dedupe: deleted $deleted own twin draft(s) for $tag — an older release already owns the tag (the same-run sibling create race, gh-2372); the caller attaches into the winner by tag (gh-1801 tolerance), nothing was lost: the twin carried only our unpublished assets" >&2
fi
exit 0

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Lazy DRAFT create for the release train's asset-upload steps (gh-1801).
#
# The train workflows (ci.yml binaries/web-spa, build-macos.yml
# build-macos-cli/build-extension) need a release object to attach assets
# to, but the release must never go live from an upload step: `fa update`
# resolves the `latest` release and hard-fails without the SIGNED
# SHA256SUMS(.sig) (bin/self_manage.dart provenance gate), which only the
# tag-run release-provenance job can upload. This script creates the
# release as a DRAFT — nothing else:
#
#   - body = scripts/release_notes.sh output (curated `## <version>`
#     CHANGELOG section → curated `## Unreleased` → conventional commits;
#     the gh-1172 curated-notes contract), with a minimal fallback —
#     never `--generate-notes` (review threads 3/7);
#   - body carries `<!-- release-draft-owner: run/<run_id>/job/<job> -->`
#     so scripts/release_draft_guard.sh can reclaim the draft on failure
#     (review threads 4/8) — matrix legs override the identity via
#     RELEASE_DRAFT_IDENTITY (e.g. binaries-linux-x64) so a failed leg's
#     guard can never match a sibling's in-flight draft;
#   - the view→create race is tolerated (`|| true`): a sibling leg or the
#     attach path may create the release between our view and create —
#     the loser just uploads into the winner's release;
#   - it NEVER publishes and NEVER flags latest: the single publish point
#     of a tag train is release-provenance's "Upload provenance assets"
#     step (`gh release edit --draft=false --latest` after SHA256SUMS.sig
#     lands). A red provenance leaves the previous release as latest —
#     safe degradation, never a provenance-less latest (v1.0.630 window).
#
# Usage: release_lazy_draft.sh <tag>
# Env: GITHUB_REPOSITORY, GITHUB_RUN_ID, GITHUB_JOB (Actions defaults),
#      RELEASE_DRAFT_IDENTITY (optional leg-suffixed override),
#      GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN.
set -euo pipefail

tag="${1:?usage: release_lazy_draft.sh <tag>}"
repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:?GITHUB_REPOSITORY must be set}"
identity="${RELEASE_DRAFT_IDENTITY:-run/${GITHUB_RUN_ID:?GITHUB_RUN_ID must be set (GitHub Actions default env)}/job/${GITHUB_JOB:?GITHUB_JOB must be set (GitHub Actions default env)}}"

# The guard greps exactly this class — validate here so a malformed
# override fails loud instead of stamping a marker the guard could never
# match (a forever-orphaned draft).
printf '%s' "$identity" | grep -Eq '^run/[0-9]+/job/[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$' || {
  echo "::error::RELEASE_DRAFT_IDENTITY '$identity' does not match 'run/<id>/job/<name>' — the draft lifecycle guard could never reclaim such a draft" >&2
  exit 1
}

# Already created (by a sibling leg, the attach path, or a previous run)?
# Drafts and published releases both resolve here — upload-only is safe.
if gh release view "$tag" --repo "$repo" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "release $tag already exists — lazy draft create skipped"
  exit 0
fi

# Body: curated notes (CHANGELOG section / Unreleased / conventional
# commits) plus the ownership marker the guard verifies before deleting.
# stderr is NOT swallowed: release_notes.sh's ::error gates (e.g. the
# duplicate-'## Unreleased' curation guard) must stay visible even when
# the minimal fallback below keeps the train moving.
notes_file="$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/release-lazy-notes.XXXXXX")"
trap 'rm -f "$notes_file"' EXIT
if ! bash "$(dirname "$0")/release_notes.sh" "$tag" >"$notes_file" ||
  [ ! -s "$notes_file" ]; then
  printf 'Release %s — see the CHANGELOG.\n' "$tag" >"$notes_file"
fi
# gh-237: bound the body BEFORE stamping the owner marker — the cap
# truncates from the TAIL, so a pre-stamped marker is cut off and the
# created draft carries no ownership proof: release_draft_guard.sh
# resolves `<unmarked>` and refuses to reclaim it, the daily sweeper
# buckets it human (the legs run with GH_TOKEN=RELEASE_PAT) and keeps
# it, dedupe ignores it — a forever-orphaned draft (gh-282). Bounded
# body (≤ 120,000) + the marker stays under the 125,000-character
# release-body cap whose overshoot HTTP-422'd `gh release create` in
# run 44680647719 (v1.0.756) and left every attach gate on the tag
# dying with "release not found".
bash "$(dirname "$0")/release_notes_cap.sh" "$notes_file"

marker="<!-- release-draft-owner: $identity -->"
grep -qF "$marker" "$notes_file" || printf '\n%s\n' "$marker" >>"$notes_file"

# gh-2026: a `gh release create` for a MISSING ref REST-mints a
# lightweight API tag with NO push event — the v0.1.408 silent class
# (issue #597). The fast legs (build-macos.yml build-extension /
# build-macos-cli) can reach this create before the attach legs
# (release-macos / release-mobile): the silent mint wins the race, every
# attach leg then finds the tag existing and skips the CI-firing
# annotated push, no tag train ever runs, and the draft is stranded
# (swept a day later — the v1.0.663 / v1.0.665 shape). When the ref is
# DEFINITELY missing, mint it through the CI-firing annotated push and
# verify the train started BEFORE creating the draft (dispatch-time call
# sites export GH_TOKEN=RELEASE_PAT for exactly this; the ci.yml tag-run
# call sites always see the tag of their own push event and never enter
# the mint). An indeterminable verdict (no origin remote, rc 128 —
# sandboxed fixtures) falls through to the plain create path.
set +e
git ls-remote --exit-code origin "refs/tags/$tag" >/dev/null 2>&1
ls_remote_rc=$?
set -e
if [ "$ls_remote_rc" -eq 2 ]; then
  bash "$(dirname "$0")/release_tag_mint.sh" "$tag"
fi

# DRAFT-first (gh-1801): a create here must never publish — the resolved
# asset list at this point can never include the signed checksums. The
# race-lost create is tolerated (the winner owns the release), but a REAL
# create failure is not (gh-237): the body was already bounded above by
# release_notes_cap.sh, so a surviving failure is a genuine API error.
create_rc=0
gh release create "$tag" \
  --repo "$repo" \
  --title "$tag" \
  --draft \
  --notes-file "$notes_file" || create_rc=$?
if [ "$create_rc" -eq 0 ]; then
  # gh-2372: the create SUCCEEDED, but a same-run sibling leg may have
  # created its own draft inside the view→create race window (GitHub
  # does not enforce one release per tag for drafts — the v1.0.760 /
  # v1.0.763 twin rot). The older (first-created) same-tag release must
  # win: self-delete OUR twin when we lost, so the caller attaches into
  # the winner and nothing rots for 24h until the sweeper. Best-effort.
  bash "$(dirname "$0")/release_draft_twin_dedupe.sh" "$tag"
  echo "✅ lazy draft ready for $tag (owner $identity) — publish is provenance-owned (gh-1801)"
  exit 0
fi
if [ "$create_rc" -ne 0 ]; then
  # gh-1801's `|| true` tolerated ONLY the view→create race — a sibling
  # leg creating the release between our view and create. gh-237 (run
  # 44680647719, v1.0.756): that swallow ALSO ate real create failures
  # (body-too-long 422), printed "✅ lazy draft ready", and failed every
  # attach gate with "release not found". Re-view: the release existing
  # NOW means we lost the race (upload into the winner's release); it
  # still being missing means the create itself failed — the leg must
  # go red, there is nothing to attach to.
  if gh release view "$tag" --repo "$repo" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "release create failed but $tag now exists — lost the view→create race, the winner owns the release"
    echo "✅ lazy draft ready for $tag (owner $identity) — publish is provenance-owned (gh-1801)"
    exit 0
  fi
  echo "::error::the draft create for $tag failed (rc $create_rc) and no concurrent release appeared — nothing to attach to; fix the create failure above (e.g. the release body exceeding the 125,000-character API cap, gh-237)" >&2
  exit 1
fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Attach assets to <tag>'s release, creating it when missing — the single
# draft-capable create path for build-macos.yml / build-mobile.yml
# (issue #282 E3 + review of #294).
#
# Race-idempotent (E3): if `gh release create` loses the view→create race
# (another job/run created the release in between), fall back to
# uploading into the winner's release instead of failing. A failed create
# would fire the job's draft lifecycle guard against the WINNER's
# in-flight draft.
#
# Ownership-stamped: the create path makes a DRAFT (gh-1801 rework: the
# release never goes live from a leg — the tag-run release-provenance job
# publishes + flags latest once the signed SHA256SUMS is attached). The
# body stamps
#   <!-- release-draft-owner: run/<run_id>/job/<job_id> -->
# and release_draft_guard.sh deletes that draft ONLY on an exact
# run+job match — never the sibling leg's mid-upload draft (daily-publish
# runs the mobile and macOS legs concurrently on the same derived tag).
# The marker is an invisible HTML comment in the body.
#
# Usage: release_attach_or_create.sh <tag> <asset> [<asset>...]
#   reads the release body from release-notes.md in the CWD (a minimal
#   body is written when the file is missing/empty)
# Env: GITHUB_REPOSITORY, GITHUB_RUN_ID, GITHUB_JOB (Actions defaults),
#      GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN.
set -euo pipefail

tag="${1:?usage: release_attach_or_create.sh <tag> <assets...>}"
repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:?GITHUB_REPOSITORY must be set}"
shift
assets=("$@")
if [ "${#assets[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
  # gh-1801 hard refusal: creating a release with zero resolved assets is
  # the `fa update` breaker (an empty `latest` 404s every
  # fa-<os>-<arch>.tar.gz until backfill — v1.0.630, 2026-10-23). Attaching
  # is the caller's only honest option when it resolved nothing — fail
  # loud here, never create empty. Pinned by
  # test/release_empty_latest_guard_test.dart.
  echo "::error::no assets to attach for $tag — refusing to create or touch a release with an empty asset list (gh-1801): resolve at least one artifact or skip the release step" >&2
  exit 1
fi

upload_all() { # exists-path: gate-guarded attach + (servable DRAFT-only) publish + latest
  # gh-2042 (AC1): every upload passes the immutability gate — on a
  # PUBLISHED release an unattached fa-* asset refuses the whole call loud,
  # an already-attached one skips, and non-fa store/DMG refreshers keep
  # their clobber-refresh contract. Drafts attach exactly as before.
  # gh-2042 (review): ONE call for the WHOLE list — the gate's contract is
  # per-call all-or-nothing ("refuse before any upload"), so per-asset
  # invocation would judge each asset against its own release-view
  # snapshot (N round-trips, a wider draft→published TOCTOU window, and a
  # partial mutation when an early benign asset uploads before a later
  # fa-* refusal).
  bash "$(dirname "$0")/release_asset_gate.sh" "$tag" "${assets[@]}"
  # Latest policy (#282 + gh-1801 rework + gh-2042): publish + latest ONLY
  # when the release can actually serve `fa update` — that means the signed
  # checksums are already on it (`fa update` hard-fails without
  # SHA256SUMS(.sig), bin/self_manage.dart provenance gate) — AND it is
  # still a DRAFT (the provenance-flip recovery window). A PUBLISHED
  # release is never re-flaged `--latest` here: on an older release that
  # would drag the latest badge (and `fa update`) backwards to a downgrade.
  if release_serves_fa_update; then
    case "$(gh release view "$tag" --repo "$repo" --json isDraft --jq .isDraft 2>/dev/null || echo false)" in
      true)
        gh release edit "$tag" --draft=false --latest --repo "$repo"
        # gh-1899: same duplicate-tag race as the tag train — a twin draft
        # minted by a sibling leg of THIS run would otherwise rot until the
        # 24h sweeper. The tag is published and servable here (the flip is
        # gated on the signed checksums), so own-run twin drafts are orphans.
        bash "$(dirname "$0")/release_draft_dedupe.sh" "$tag" \
          || echo "::warning::gh-1899 twin-draft dedupe failed — the release is published and servable, so this is cleanup noise only; the 24h sweeper remains the backstop"
        ;;
      *)
        echo "release $tag is already published — publish/latest flip skipped (gh-2042: latest never moves backwards; the signed SHA256SUMS re-upload is release-provenance's job)"
        ;;
    esac
  else
    echo "release $tag is not yet servable (no SHA256SUMS on it) — publish+latest left to the release-provenance step (gh-1801)"
  fi
}

# fa-update servability = the signed checksums are on the release. Every
# fa-* archive alone is NOT enough: `fa update` fetches SHA256SUMS(.sig)
# and aborts when either is missing (bin/self_manage.dart).
release_serves_fa_update() {
  local names
  names=$(gh release view "$tag" --repo "$repo" --json assets --jq '.assets[].name' 2>/dev/null || true)
  printf '%s\n' "$names" | grep -qE '^SHA256SUMS(\.sig)?$'
}

if gh release view "$tag" --repo "$repo" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  upload_all
  echo "✅ attached ${#assets[@]} asset(s) to existing release $tag"
  exit 0
fi

# Body: prepared notes (CHANGELOG section / conventional-commit fallback)
# plus the ownership marker the guard verifies before deleting.
notes="release-notes.md"
[ -s "$notes" ] || printf 'Release %s — see the CHANGELOG.\n' "$tag" > "$notes"
bash "$(dirname "$0")/release_notes_cap.sh" "$notes"

# gh-237: the cap runs BEFORE the owner marker is stamped — it
# truncates from the TAIL, so a pre-stamped marker is cut off and the
# created draft carries no ownership proof: release_draft_guard.sh
# resolves `<unmarked>` and refuses to reclaim it, the daily sweeper
# buckets it human (the legs run with GH_TOKEN=RELEASE_PAT) and keeps
# it, dedupe ignores it — a forever-orphaned draft (gh-282). Bounded
# body (≤ 120,000) + the marker stays under GitHub's 125,000-character
# release-body cap whose overshoot HTTP-422'd the create in run
# 44680647719 (v1.0.756).
marker="<!-- release-draft-owner: run/${GITHUB_RUN_ID:?GITHUB_RUN_ID must be set (GitHub Actions default env)}/job/${GITHUB_JOB:?GITHUB_JOB must be set (GitHub Actions default env)} -->"
grep -qF "$marker" "$notes" || printf '\n%s\n' "$marker" >> "$notes"

# A `gh release create` for a MISSING tag mints a lightweight API tag:
# no push event → no ci.yml tag run → no publish/binaries (the v0.1.408
# silent class, issue #597). If the ref is absent, mint it as an
# ANNOTATED tag and push it with the PAT the job already carries
# (GH_TOKEN=RELEASE_PAT in build-macos) so the tag CI fires. The mint
# itself (GH_TOKEN guard, persisted-checkout-extraheader strip, push,
# train-start verification) lives in scripts/release_tag_mint.sh —
# gh-2026: the v1.0.663 / v1.0.665 minted pushes rode actions/checkout's
# persisted GITHUB_TOKEN extraheader (it outranks the URL credentials),
# GitHub suppresses workflow triggers for GITHUB_TOKEN pushes, no tag run
# ever existed on those refs, and the drafts rotted behind green legs.
# A mint whose train does not start now fails loud BEFORE any draft is
# created, so the leg goes red and the failure-path draft guard has
# nothing to reclaim.
# Gate on the DEFINITE missing verdict (ls-remote --exit-code rc 2):
# sandboxes without an origin remote fatal with 128 — indeterminable
# falls through to the plain create path (test fixtures rely on it).
set +e
git ls-remote --exit-code origin "refs/tags/$tag" >/dev/null 2>&1
ls_remote_rc=$?
set -e
if [ "$ls_remote_rc" -eq 2 ]; then
  bash "$(dirname "$0")/release_tag_mint.sh" "$tag"
fi

# Bare vX.Y.Z title (#282): matches the tag, matches pub.dev. gh-1801
# rework: the create is DRAFT-ONLY. Whatever this leg resolved
# (AAB/IPA/store APKs, DMGs/zips) is not the signed provenance `fa update`
# demands — a leg that arrives first must never publish the release, let
# alone flag it latest (threads 2/6). The draft is ownership-stamped (the
# marker below) so this job's draft lifecycle guard reclaims it on
# failure; the tag-run binaries job attaches the CLI assets into it and
# release-provenance (ci.yml) publishes + flags latest once SHA256SUMS.sig
# is on board.
if gh release create "$tag" \
  --repo "$repo" \
  --title "$tag" \
  --draft \
  --notes-file "$notes" \
  "${assets[@]}"; then
  # gh-2372: the create SUCCEEDED, but a same-run sibling leg may have
  # created its own draft inside the view→create race window (GitHub
  # does not enforce one release per tag for drafts — the v1.0.760 /
  # v1.0.763 twin rot). The older (first-created) same-tag release must
  # win: self-delete OUR twin when we lost — these assets then upload
  # into the winner by tag on a rerun-attach, and nothing rots for 24h
  # until the sweeper. Best-effort.
  bash "$(dirname "$0")/release_draft_twin_dedupe.sh" "$tag"
  echo "✅ created draft release $tag with ${#assets[@]} asset(s) — publish is provenance-owned (gh-1801)"
  exit 0
fi

# E3 idempotency: the create may have lost the view→create race — the
# winner's release now exists. Attach instead of failing (a failing
# create would fire the guard against the winner's in-flight draft).
if gh release view "$tag" --repo "$repo" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  upload_all
  echo "✅ lost the create race — attached ${#assets[@]} asset(s) to the concurrently created release $tag"
  exit 0
fi

echo "::error::release create for $tag failed and no concurrent release appeared — see the step log above" >&2
exit 1

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Daily release-draft sweeper (issue #282), rides daily-publish.yml:
#
#   - lists DRAFT releases older than $SWEEP_MAX_AGE_SECONDS (default 24h);
#   - deletes stale drafts created by the pipeline (author.type == Bot, a
#     *[bot] login, the repo's machine account (DAILY_PUBLISH_ASSIGNEE,
#     default ai-teammate — gh-2287: its drafts (ai-gh-*/ai-pr-*) are
#     User-typed and marker-less but machine-created), OR the body
#     carries a well-formed `release-draft-owner: run/<id>/job/<job>`
#     marker — the exact shape
#     release_lazy_draft.sh / release_attach_or_create.sh stamp and
#     release_draft_guard.sh parses; since the drafts are created with
#     GH_TOKEN=RELEASE_PAT the API author is the PAT's human owner, so
#     the marker is the only ownership proof, gh-2008. Prose that merely
#     MENTIONS the substring or a malformed marker is NOT ownership —
#     those drafts stay human/kept, E1) — draft assets are unpublished by
#     definition and published releases are the artifact store, so
#     deletion is safe (issue #282 E2). The git tag is never touched;
#   - stale HUMAN drafts are listed in the summary, never deleted (E1);
#   - fresh drafts (<24h) are counted, never touched — an in-flight run
#     may legitimately own them. EXCEPTION (gh-2318): a fresh draft with a
#     well-formed release-draft-owner marker is RECLAIMED immediately when
#     its owner run completed, no ci.yml push train on the tag is still
#     queued/in-flight, and the tag's newest concluded ci.yml push train
#     failed with release-provenance SKIPPED (the publish point is
#     unreachable — rerun --failed cannot resurrect skipped jobs, so
#     nobody will ever publish it; the same criterion as ci.yml's gh-2230
#     train-draft-guard, which only sees drafts visible at train end).
#     A rerunnable (FAILED) provenance keeps the draft as the rerun
#     --failed recovery vessel (gh-1899) until it goes stale below;
#   - files ONE deduplicated, self-closing issue (label release-hygiene)
#     whenever anything stale was found — a comment on the open issue
#     instead of a duplicate, auto-closed again once a sweep comes up
#     clean (same convention as nightly.yml / daily_publish_report.sh).
#
# ── orphaned twin drafts are lifecycle-managed hygiene (gh-2372) ───────────
# A MARKED pipeline draft whose tag ALREADY carries a PUBLISHED release is
# a proven orphan twin of the same-run sibling view→create race (v1.0.760:
# the build-extension draft won + was published, the build-macos-cli twin
# rotted 43h and was swept with the misleading "a `gh release create` step
# died" prose; v1.0.763's twin rotted while counted "fresh"). No run can
# ever publish or attach into such a draft — uploads resolve the published
# object by tag — and release_draft_twin_dedupe.sh now self-deletes the
# loser at create time, so any twin the sweep still sees is a best-effort
# leftover. The sweep reclaims these drafts IMMEDIATELY (fresh or stale)
# as routine hygiene (gh-236 convention: visible in the summary, never a
# stale-draft finding — a residual twin must not re-file the recurring
# issue), and the clean-sweep auto-close names the reclaims. Ownership
# proof stays required: an UNMARKED author-bot draft on a published tag
# keeps the bot-bucket finding (no marker → no ownership → existing
# behavior).
#
# ── artefact-cache drafts have their own lifecycle (gh-236) ────────────────
# The machine loop (dmtools-agents factory: timerAutoCommitAndSave.js →
# releaseArtefacts.uploadRawFile → github_get_or_create_draft_release, tag
# template `ai-{ticketKey}`) writes every fa leg's session/output snapshots
# as assets of a per-ticket DRAFT release `ai-gh-<n>` / `ai-pr-<n>`, created
# with the ai-teammate token — User-typed, marker-less, no Actions run owns
# it. Those drafts are caches by design (never published, assets
# best-effort), NOT failed release-train drafts — but without a lifecycle
# they rotted 24h, were swept as generic bot-bucket findings, and re-filed
# the recurring sweep issue every day (gh-2287 → gh-2318 → gh-236). The
# guard: a machine-account draft whose tag matches `ai-(gh|pr)-<digits>` is
#   - RECLAIMED NOW, any age, when the ticket entity is `closed` — a closed
#     cycle never resumes (a reopened ticket starts a fresh session; the
#     pack's restore path is non-fatal and recreates the cache on "first
#     run"), so the draft is provably garbage the moment the cycle ends;
#   - swept by the existing 24h backstop when the ticket is still open (a
#     parked leg — the cache is recreated if the leg resumes);
#   - kept untouched while the ticket is open and the draft is fresh (an
#     in-flight leg may be writing snapshots into it);
#   - KEPT on any ticket-state lookup failure (never delete blind) — only
#     the 24h backstop then applies.
# The class is EXCLUDED from the sweep-issue finding counters: reclaiming a
# lifecycle-managed cache is routine hygiene, not a stale-draft finding, so
# the issue auto-closes when only cache traffic remains. Human-authored
# `ai-*` drafts are NOT lifecycle-managed (E1 holds — they stay listed,
# kept), and machine-authored non-matching drafts (e.g. a machine-authored
# `vX.Y.Z` train draft) stay in the bot bucket and remain findings.
#
# Drafts are deleted by release id via the API: a draft may carry an empty
# tag_name, which makes every tag-based `gh release delete` ambiguous.
#
# Env: GITHUB_REPOSITORY, GH_TOKEN, SWEEP_MAX_AGE_SECONDS (default 86400),
#      SWEEP_LABEL (default release-hygiene).
set -euo pipefail

repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:?GITHUB_REPOSITORY must be set}"
max_age="${SWEEP_MAX_AGE_SECONDS:-86400}"
label="${SWEEP_LABEL:-release-hygiene}"
# The repo's machine-account identity (same env + default as
# daily_publish_report.sh): drafts authored by it are pipeline-created —
# gh-2287: the ai-teammate factory's drafts (ai-gh-*/ai-pr-*) are User-typed
# and marker-less, so author-only Bot detection bucketed them as human and
# they rotted forever while the sweep issue never auto-closed.
assignee="${DAILY_PUBLISH_ASSIGNEE:-ai-teammate}"
title="[daily-publish] stale release drafts swept"
daily_url="${GITHUB_SERVER_URL:-https://github.com}/$repo/actions/runs/${GITHUB_RUN_ID:-manual}"

# ── failed-train diagnosis (gh-2105 + gh-2318) ──────────────────────────────
# The staged draft's publish owner is the TAG TRAIN (ci.yml's push run on
# the tag ref — release-provenance is the sole publish point, gh-1801).
# Diagnose <tag>'s newest CONCLUDED failed ci.yml push train; prints one
# TSV row:
#
#   train_id <TAB> conclusion <TAB> url <TAB> failed_jobs <TAB> prov_conclusion <TAB> in_flight
#
# `failed_jobs` names the train's failure-concluded jobs (the gh-2105 issue
# prose). `prov_conclusion` is the release-provenance job's OWN conclusion —
# "skipped" means the publish point is UNREACHABLE (`rerun --failed` never
# resurrects skipped jobs — the gh-2230 train-guard criterion), "failure"
# means it is rerunnable (the staged draft is the `rerun --failed` recovery
# vessel, gh-1899 — the stale 24h sweep reclaims it if the train is never
# recovered). `in_flight` is "in_flight" when ANY fetched ci.yml push run
# on the tag has a null conclusion (queued or in progress), "none" when all
# have concluded, and "unknown" if that check fails; the fresh-draft reclaim
# keeps unless it is explicitly "none", because a live train may still
# publish even when an older train failed. The publish-point job is matched
# by its ci.yml `name:` —
# "Sign release checksums" (pinned by test/release_stale_draft_reclaim_test.dart,
# gh-2318 group; update both together). Empty output = no failed train /
# lookup failed; every consumer degrades fail-safe (keep), and nothing
# here may gate the stale >24h delete (the diagnosis is never a
# precondition — gh-2105).
train_diagnosis() {
  local tag="$1" train_json failed_train train_id jobs_json in_flight
  train_json=$(gh run list --repo "$repo" --workflow ci.yml \
    --branch "$tag" --event push --limit 5 \
    --json databaseId,conclusion,url 2>/dev/null || echo "[]")
  in_flight=$(printf '%s' "$train_json" | jq -r '
    if any(.[]; .conclusion == null) then "in_flight" else "none" end
  ' 2>/dev/null || echo "unknown")
  failed_train=$(printf '%s' "$train_json" | jq -cr '
    ([.[] | select(.conclusion != "success" and .conclusion != null)][0]
      | if . == null then empty else
          {c: .conclusion, u: (.url // ""), i: .databaseId}
        end)' 2>/dev/null || echo "")
  [ -n "$failed_train" ] || return 0
  train_id=$(printf '%s' "$failed_train" | jq -r '.i // ""' 2>/dev/null || echo "")
  jobs_json=$(gh run view "$train_id" --repo "$repo" --json jobs 2>/dev/null || echo "")
  printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s' \
    "$train_id" \
    "$(printf '%s' "$failed_train" | jq -r '.c // "unknown"' 2>/dev/null || echo "unknown")" \
    "$(printf '%s' "$failed_train" | jq -r '.u // ""' 2>/dev/null || echo "")" \
    "$(printf '%s' "$jobs_json" | jq -r '[.jobs[] | select(.conclusion == "failure") | .name] | join(", ")' 2>/dev/null || echo "")" \
    "$(printf '%s' "$jobs_json" | jq -r '([.jobs[] | select(.name == "Sign release checksums")][0].conclusion // "")' 2>/dev/null || echo "")" \
    "$in_flight"
}


gh label create "$label" --repo "$repo" --color B60205 \
  --description "Auto-filed by the release-draft sweeper" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true

# ── inventory ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# gh api --paginate emits one JSON array per page; the jq stream filter
# flattens them all. The roster is fetched ONCE and read twice: the draft
# rows below, plus (gh-2372) the set of tags that already carry a PUBLISHED
# release — the twin-orphan criterion. Bucketing happens in jq so the whole
# rule is reviewable in one place:
#   artifacts (machine account + ai-(gh|pr)-<n> tag — gh-236)
#                    -> lifecycle-managed: reclaim at cycle end / 24h
#                    backstop / keep in flight; NEVER a sweep finding
#   stale + pipeline (bot author, the machine account, or well-formed
#                    release-draft-owner: run/<id>/job/<job>
#                    marker in the body) -> delete, name the marker run
#   stale + human (no marker)          -> keep, list
#   fresh                              -> untouched, EXCEPT the gh-2318
#                    reclaim: a marked draft whose owner run completed and
#                    whose tag's train failed with release-provenance
#                    SKIPPED (publish point unreachable) is deleted NOW
roster=$(gh api --paginate "repos/$repo/releases")
# gh-2372: the tags that already carry a PUBLISHED release. Multi-page
# safe: the filter runs per page-array, so the joins are re-joined in bash.
published_tags=$(printf '%s' "$roster" \
  | jq -r '[.[] | select(.draft == false) | (.tag_name // "")] | join(" ")' \
  | tr '\n' ' ')
drafts=$(printf '%s' "$roster" | jq -r --argjson maxage "$max_age" --arg assignee "$assignee" '
  [ .[] | select(.draft == true)
    | { stale: ((now - (.created_at | fromdateiso8601)) > $maxage),
        bucket: (
          # gh-236 first: the machine loop artefact-cache class, keyed on
          # the machine account AND the `ai-{ticketKey}` tag shape the
          # factory releaseArtefacts.buildTag() produces (lowercased,
          # non-alnum to '-', so `GH-2288` becomes `ai-gh-2288`,
          # `pr-2293` becomes `ai-pr-2293`). Human-authored ai-* drafts and
          # machine-authored vX.Y.Z drafts never match and fall through to
          # the buckets below.
          if (((.author.login // "") == $assignee)
              and ((.tag_name // "") | test("^ai-(gh|pr)-[0-9]+$")))
          then "artifacts"
          elif ((now - (.created_at | fromdateiso8601)) > $maxage)
          then (if ((.author.type // "User") == "Bot"
                    or ((.author.login // "") | test("\\[bot\\]$"))
                    or ((.author.login // "") == $assignee)
                    or ((.body // "") | test("release-draft-owner: run/[0-9]+/job/")))
               then "bot" else "human" end)
          else "fresh" end),
        tag: (.tag_name // "(untagged)"),
        id: (.id | tostring),
        created: (.created_at // "?"),
        author: (.author.login // "unknown"),
        # Exact creating run parsed from the ownership marker ("" for
        # non-marker drafts) — the creating run executed on main, so a
        # tag-ref run lookup cannot find it (gh-2008). The array wrapper
        # keeps exactly one value: a bare capture(...)? on a non-matching
        # body yields an EMPTY stream, and an empty field would drop the
        # whole draft row from the object stream.
        run: ([ (.body // "")
                | capture("release-draft-owner: run/(?<run>[0-9]+)/")?
                | .run ]
              | .[0] // "") } ]
  | sort_by(.created)[]
  # Column order matters: `read` collapses runs of whitespace IFS chars, so
  # the only possibly-EMPTY field (.run — marker-less drafts) must stay
  # LAST; .stale sits before it (gh-236: the artifacts branch branches on it).
  | [ .bucket, .tag, .id, .created, .author, .stale, .run ] | @tsv')

deleted=""
deleted_tags=""
deleted_count=0
failed_trains=0
# gh-2318: fresh (<24h) pipeline drafts reclaimed early — provably
# never-publishable (completed owner, failed train with skipped
# release-provenance). Tracked separately from the >24h sweep deletions.
reclaimed=""
reclaimed_tags=""
reclaimed_count=0
humans=""
human_tags=""
fresh_count=0
# gh-236: machine-loop artefact-cache drafts — lifecycle-managed, NOT
# sweep findings (reclaiming a cache whose ticket cycle ended is routine
# hygiene; the issue must auto-close when only cache traffic remains).
#   reclaimed at cycle end (ticket closed, any age) / swept by the 24h
#   backstop (ticket still open / state unknown) / kept (fresh + open).
art_reclaimed=""
art_reclaimed_tags=""
art_reclaimed_count=0
art_swept=""
art_swept_tags=""
art_swept_count=0
art_kept_tags=""
art_kept_count=0
# gh-2372: orphaned twin drafts (marked draft, tag already published) —
# lifecycle-managed hygiene like the artefact caches above: reclaimed at
# ANY age, visible in the summary, never a stale-draft finding.
twins=""
twin_tags=""
twin_count=0

while IFS=$'\t' read -r bucket tag id created author stale marker_run; do
  [ -n "$bucket" ] || continue
  # ── gh-2372 twin pre-check (before the bucket dispatch) ────────────────
  # A MARKED draft whose tag already carries a PUBLISHED release is a
  # proven orphan twin of the sibling create race: nothing can ever
  # publish or attach into it (uploads resolve the published object by
  # tag), and release_draft_twin_dedupe.sh now self-deletes the loser at
  # create time — anything the sweep still sees is a best-effort
  # leftover. Reclaimed at ANY age as routine hygiene, never a finding.
  # The artifacts bucket is excluded (lifecycle-managed above); unmarked
  # drafts have no ownership proof and stay in their buckets (E1).
  twin_published=false
  case " $published_tags " in *" $tag "*) twin_published=true ;; esac
  if [ "$twin_published" = "true" ] && [ -n "$marker_run" ] \
    && [ "$bucket" != "artifacts" ] && [ "$tag" != "(untagged)" ]; then
    gh api -X DELETE "repos/$repo/releases/$id" >/dev/null
    twin_count=$((twin_count + 1))
    twin_tags="$twin_tags $tag"
    run_url="${GITHUB_SERVER_URL:-https://github.com}/$repo/actions/runs/$marker_run"
    twins="$twins- \`$tag\` — created $created by @$author; creating run: $run_url\n  - reclaimed as an orphaned twin draft: the tag already carries a PUBLISHED release, so no run could ever publish or attach into this one (the same-run sibling create race won — gh-2372; self-deduped at create by release_draft_twin_dedupe.sh, this sweep is the backstop). Routine hygiene (gh-236 convention) — not a stale-draft finding.\n"
    continue
  fi
  case "$bucket" in
    artifacts)
      # gh-236: the machine loop's per-ticket artefact-cache draft
      # (`ai-gh-<n>` / `ai-pr-<n>` — timerAutoCommitAndSave.js snapshot
      # storage). The tag shape was validated by the jq bucket rule, so
      # `gh #<num>` / `pr #<num>` parsing below is total. State lookup:
      # the issues REST API serves PRs too (state=closed covers merged).
      # Any lookup failure yields an empty state — fail-safe: no early
      # reclaim, only the 24h backstop below may delete.
      rest="${tag#ai-}"
      kind="${rest%%-*}"
      num="${rest##*-}"
      state=$(gh api "repos/$repo/issues/$num" 2>/dev/null \
        | jq -r '.state // ""' 2>/dev/null || echo "")
      if [ "$state" = "closed" ]; then
        gh api -X DELETE "repos/$repo/releases/$id" >/dev/null
        art_reclaimed_count=$((art_reclaimed_count + 1))
        art_reclaimed="$art_reclaimed- \`$tag\` — created $created by @$author; ticket cycle ended (\`$kind #$num\` closed) — reclaimed at cycle end, no 24h wait: a closed cycle never resumes and the cache is recreated on any future first run (gh-236)\n"
        art_reclaimed_tags="$art_reclaimed_tags $tag"
      elif [ "$stale" = "true" ]; then
        gh api -X DELETE "repos/$repo/releases/$id" >/dev/null
        art_swept_count=$((art_swept_count + 1))
        art_swept="$art_swept- \`$tag\` — created $created by @$author; swept after 24h with the ticket still open or its state unknown (parked leg — the cache is recreated if the leg resumes; gh-236)\n"
        art_swept_tags="$art_swept_tags $tag"
      else
        art_kept_count=$((art_kept_count + 1))
        art_kept_tags="$art_kept_tags $tag"
      fi
      ;;
    fresh)
      # gh-2318: "fresh — untouched" is right while an in-flight run may
      # own the draft, but a fresh draft can already be PROVABLY
      # never-publishable: the v1.0.739 shape — a daily-child staging leg
      # minted the tag (release_tag_mint.sh) and staged the draft, the
      # freshly fired train failed upstream of release-provenance, and the
      # gh-2230 train-draft-guard either ran before the draft existed (a
      # long attach leg created it later) or kept it while its owner was
      # still in-flight. Nothing re-examined such a draft with train
      # knowledge, so it rotted the full 24h and re-filed the recurring
      # sweep issue. Apply the train guard's EXACT criterion here —
      # reclaim only a well-formed-marker draft whose owner run COMPLETED,
      # whose tag has NO queued/in-flight ci.yml push train, and whose
      # newest concluded ci.yml push train failed with release-provenance
      # SKIPPED (rerun --failed cannot resurrect skipped jobs — nobody
      # will ever publish it). Fail-safe keeps mirror the train guard:
      # unmarked/human drafts (E1), an in-flight owner run (possibly
      # mid-upload), ANY queued/in-flight tag train (it may still publish
      # even when an older train failed), a rerunnable FAILED provenance
      # (that draft stays the `rerun --failed` recovery vessel, gh-1899,
      # until the stale sweep), any lookup failure (never delete blind),
      # and untagged drafts (no train to diagnose).
      if [ -n "$marker_run" ] && [ "$tag" != "(untagged)" ]; then
        owner_status=$(gh run view "$marker_run" --repo "$repo" --json status 2>/dev/null \
          | jq -r '.status // empty' 2>/dev/null || echo "")
        if [ "$owner_status" = "completed" ]; then
          diag=$(train_diagnosis "$tag")
          train_url_found=$(printf '%s' "$diag" | cut -f3)
          failed_jobs=$(printf '%s' "$diag" | cut -f4)
          prov_conclusion=$(printf '%s' "$diag" | cut -f5)
          train_conclusion=$(printf '%s' "$diag" | cut -f2)
          train_in_flight=$(printf '%s' "$diag" | cut -f6)
          if [ -n "$diag" ] && [ "$prov_conclusion" = "skipped" ] \
            && [ "$train_in_flight" = "none" ]; then
            gh api -X DELETE "repos/$repo/releases/$id" >/dev/null
            reclaimed_count=$((reclaimed_count + 1))
            failed_trains=$((failed_trains + 1))
            run_url="${GITHUB_SERVER_URL:-https://github.com}/$repo/actions/runs/$marker_run"
            train_line="  - tag train: ${train_url_found:-<url unavailable>} concluded ${train_conclusion:-unknown} — the staged draft was never published (release-provenance, the sole publish point, is gated behind the tag train; a superseded failed train is never rerun — verify_pubdev_release.sh heals the LATEST tag only)"
            [ -n "$failed_jobs" ] && train_line="$train_line; failed jobs: $failed_jobs"
            reclaimed="$reclaimed- \`$tag\` — created $created by @$author; creating run: $run_url\n  - reclaimed early: the draft is younger than $((max_age / 3600))h but its publish point is unreachable (failed train, skipped release-provenance — rerun --failed cannot resurrect skipped jobs), so no in-flight run can own it and nobody will ever publish it (gh-2318)\n$train_line\n"
            reclaimed_tags="$reclaimed_tags $tag"
            continue
          fi
        fi
      fi
      fresh_count=$((fresh_count + 1))
      ;;
    human)
      humans="$humans- \`$tag\` — created $created by @$author (human draft: listed, kept)\n"
      human_tags="$human_tags $tag"
      ;;
    bot)
      gh api -X DELETE "repos/$repo/releases/$id" >/dev/null
      deleted_count=$((deleted_count + 1))
      # Name the creating run so a RECURRING stuck draft points at its
      # broken step instead of rotting silently (AC2). Marker drafts name
      # it exactly (the stamping scripts write run/<id>); untagged
      # author-bot drafts fall back to the newest run on the tag ref;
      # dispatch-time drafts have no run on their ref — then say so.
      run_url=""
      if [ -n "$marker_run" ]; then
        run_url="${GITHUB_SERVER_URL:-https://github.com}/$repo/actions/runs/$marker_run"
      elif [ "$tag" != "(untagged)" ]; then
        run_url=$(gh run list --repo "$repo" --branch "$tag" --limit 1 \
          --json url --jq '.[0].url // empty' 2>/dev/null || true)
      fi
      if [ -z "$run_url" ]; then
        if [ "$author" = "$assignee" ]; then
          # gh-2287: a machine-account draft carries no marker (the
          # automation created it with its own token, outside this repo's
          # runners) — name the account as the creator; the dispatch-time
          # "creating step died mid-run" prose below would misdirect the
          # RCA (gh-2105 class) — nothing died.
          run_url="the @$assignee automation loop (machine-account draft — created outside this repo's runners, no Actions run owns it)"
        else
          run_url="no run on ref \`$tag\` (dispatch-time draft — the creating step died mid-run)"
        fi
      fi
      # gh-2105: the staging draft's publish owner is the TAG TRAIN
      # (ci.yml's push run on the tag ref — release-provenance is the
      # sole publish point, gh-1801). When that train failed, the
      # creating run named above is NOT the broken step — the train is,
      # and a superseded failed train is never rerun
      # (verify_pubdev_release.sh heals the LATEST tag only). Name it
      # (URL + conclusion + failed jobs) so the sweep issue points at
      # the true blocker. Any lookup failure degrades to the static
      # prose below — the delete + issue filing must never depend on
      # the diagnosis.
      train_line=""
      if [ "$tag" != "(untagged)" ]; then
        diag=$(train_diagnosis "$tag")
        if [ -n "$diag" ]; then
          train_conclusion=$(printf '%s' "$diag" | cut -f2)
          train_url_found=$(printf '%s' "$diag" | cut -f3)
          failed_jobs=$(printf '%s' "$diag" | cut -f4)
          failed_trains=$((failed_trains + 1))
          train_line="  - tag train: ${train_url_found:-<url unavailable>} concluded ${train_conclusion:-unknown} — the staged draft was never published (release-provenance, the sole publish point, is gated behind the tag train; a superseded failed train is never rerun — verify_pubdev_release.sh heals the LATEST tag only)"
          [ -n "$failed_jobs" ] && train_line="$train_line; failed jobs: $failed_jobs"
          train_line="$train_line\n"
        fi
      fi
      deleted="$deleted- \`$tag\` — created $created by @$author; creating run: $run_url\n$train_line"
      deleted_tags="$deleted_tags $tag"
      ;;
  esac
done <<< "$drafts"

# ── issue lifecycle (dedup + self-closing) ─────────────────────────────────
find_open_issue() { # echoes the issue number of the open sweep issue, or nothing
  gh issue list --repo "$repo" --state open --label "$label" \
    --limit 100 --json number,title --jq '.[] | [.number, .title] | @tsv' 2>/dev/null \
    | while IFS=$'\t' read -r n t; do
        if [ "$t" = "$title" ]; then echo "$n"; fi
      done | head -1
}

same_run_issues() { # gh-2359 AC3: open issues already filed from THIS run
  # The run URL is the join key (the leg-filer embeds the same
  # **Daily run:**/**Sweep run:** URL): a sweep finding and a leg failure
  # from one daily run (the #2336/#2337 shape) share roots even though
  # their error signatures never match.
  # gh itself has no --arg flag — the filter runs through real jq, exactly
  # like this script's `gh api --paginate … | jq -r --arg …` draft lookups.
  gh issue list --repo "$repo" --state open --limit 200 --json number,body \
    2>/dev/null \
    | jq -r --arg run_url "$daily_url" \
      '.[] | select((.body // "") | contains($run_url)) | .number' \
    || true
}

stale_count=$((deleted_count + reclaimed_count + $(printf '%s' "$humans" | grep -c . || true) ))

if [ "$stale_count" -gt 0 ]; then
  body=$(mktemp)
  {
    echo "**Sweep run:** $daily_url"
    echo "**Swept:** $deleted_count stale pipeline-created draft(s) older than $((max_age / 3600))h"
    printf '%b' "$deleted"
    # gh-2318: fresh drafts reclaimed early — their publish point is
    # unreachable, so the 24h wait would only delay the inevitable and
    # keep the sweep issue recurring (see the branch comment for the
    # full fail-safe keep list).
    if [ "$reclaimed_count" -gt 0 ]; then
      echo
      echo "**Reclaimed early (<$((max_age / 3600))h):** $reclaimed_count fresh pipeline draft(s) whose publish point is unreachable (gh-2318)"
      printf '%b' "$reclaimed"
    fi
    [ -n "$humans" ] && { echo; echo "**Kept (human drafts, listed not deleted — E1):**"; printf '%b' "$humans"; }
    # gh-236: cache lifecycle activity rides the filed issue for
    # visibility — in its own section, with the release-failure prose
    # never attached (nothing died, nothing failed to publish). It does
    # NOT contribute to the finding count above.
    if [ "$((art_reclaimed_count + art_swept_count))" -gt 0 ]; then
      echo
      echo "**Artefact-cache drafts (machine-loop \`ai-gh-*\`/\`ai-pr-*\` caches — lifecycle-managed, not release failures):** $art_reclaimed_count reclaimed at cycle end, $art_swept_count swept after 24h"
      printf '%b' "$art_reclaimed"
      printf '%b' "$art_swept"
    fi
    # gh-2372: orphaned twin reclaims ride the filed issue for visibility —
    # own section, hygiene prose, never part of the finding counters.
    if [ "$twin_count" -gt 0 ]; then
      echo

tools.name: read
tools.description:
Read the contents of a text file or image. Text output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large text files. Images are returned as base64 content. Video files route to a video-capable model when one is available (the bytes are attached or described with attribution); otherwise a note names how to configure video reading.

## Path selectors

Append a trailing selector to `path` to read exactly the lines you need:

- `:N` — start at line N (1-indexed), through end of file. `:N-` is the same.
- `:A-B` — inclusive line range (`:A..B` works too).
- `:A+C` — C lines starting at A.
- `:R1,R2,…` — multiple ranges, sorted and merged (`:5-16,960-973`); blocks are joined with a `…` separator and ranges past end of file are reported as skipped.
- `:raw` — verbatim content: no line numbers, no hashline header, no notices. Combine as `:raw:50-100` or `:50-100:raw`.

Do not combine `offset`/`limit` with a path selector. Selectors only apply to text files (not images).

## Archives

Read inside `.zip`, `.tar`, `.tar.gz`/`.tgz` files: `archive.zip` lists the root, `archive.zip:dir/` lists a directory, `archive.zip:inner/file.txt` reads a member (selectors apply, e.g. `archive.zip:inner/file.txt:50-60`). Binary members return a note.

## SQLite databases

When the host supports it, `.db`/`.db3`/`.sqlite`/`.sqlite3` paths read as databases: `data.db` lists tables, `data.db:table` shows the schema plus sample rows, `data.db:table:key` fetches one row by primary key (or rowid), `data.db:table?limit=20&offset=40&order=col:desc&where=...` pages a table, and `data.db?q=SELECT ...` runs a raw read-only query.

## Hashline mode

Set hashline=true to prefix lines with line numbers and a [path#TAG] content-hash header for anchoring hashline edit patches (line numbers stay correct on ranged reads). Suppressed by `:raw`.

tools.name: write
tools.description: Write content to a file, creating parent directories as needed. Overwrites the file if it already exists.

tools.name: edit
tools.description:
Edit a file in one of two modes.

## Exact-match mode: `path` + `oldText` + `newText`

Replace an exact text occurrence. `oldText` must match exactly (including indentation and newlines) and occur exactly once in the file. Prefer this over `write` for small, precise changes to existing files; read the file first to get the exact text.

## Hashline mode: `patch`

A hashline patch names lines to replace, delete, or insert at by number, bound to a `[PATH#TAG]` content-hash header — precise line addressing without re-quoting file text. To author one, first `read` the file with `hashline=true`: it returns a `[PATH#TAG]` header and `LINE:TEXT` rows. Rule of thumb: a header ending in `:` is followed by `+` body rows; `DEL` has no body.

<headers>
Every file section starts with `[PATH#TAG]`. `TAG` = the 4-hex snapshot tag from your latest hashline `read` or edit response, REQUIRED on every section. Create new files with `write`; hashline only edits existing files. One patch may carry several `[PATH#TAG]` sections (different files); all sections apply or none do.
</headers>

<ops>
`SWAP N.=M:` — replace original lines N.=M with the body rows below. INCLUSIVE — line M is consumed too.
`DEL N.=M` — delete original lines N.=M. No body.
`INS.PRE N:` — insert the body rows immediately before line N.
`INS.POST N:` — insert the body rows immediately after line N.
`INS.HEAD:` / `INS.TAIL:` — insert the body rows at the very start / end of the file.
Single line: `SWAP N.=N:` / `DEL N`. The range is the ORIGINAL lines you touch; body length is irrelevant (replacing 1 line with 10 is still `SWAP N.=N:`).
</ops>

<body-rows>
Body rows appear only under a `:` header. Every body row is `+TEXT` — add a literal line `TEXT`, verbatim (leading whitespace kept); `+` alone adds a blank line. No other row kind. NEVER write `-old` or a bare/context line. To keep a line, leave it out of every range. Literal lines starting with `-`/`+` still need the body prefix: Markdown `- item` → `+- item`, `+ item` → `++ item`.
</body-rows>

<rules>
- Line numbers + `[PATH#TAG]` header come from your latest hashline `read` (`LINE:TEXT` rows) or edit response.
- Numbers refer to the ORIGINAL file; never shift as hunks apply.
- They die with the call: every applied edit mints a fresh `#TAG` and renumbers — anchor the next edit on the edit response or a fresh hashline `read`.
- Touch only lines your latest `read` literally displayed as `LINE:TEXT`; the tag certifies the snapshot, not your memory. A hunk anchored on a line you never displayed is REJECTED — re-`read` that range first.
- Never start or end a range mid-expression or mid-block.
- Indent body rows exactly for the depth they should live at.
- On a stale-tag rejection or any surprising result: STOP and re-`read` before further edits.
- One hunk per range; body = final content, never an old/new pair.
- Ranges cover ONLY lines whose content changes. Never widen over unchanged lines — a stale wide range shreds everything it spans.
- Pure additions use `INS.PRE` / `INS.POST` / `INS.HEAD` / `INS.TAIL`, never a widened `SWAP`.
- Non-adjacent changes = separate hunks; untouched lines stay out of every range.
- NEVER format/restyle code with this tool; run the project formatter instead.
</rules>

<example>
Original (the exact shape `read` with `hashline=true` returns):
```
[greet.py#A1B2]
1:def greet(name):
2:    msg = "Hello, " + name
3:    print(msg)
4:greet("world")
```

Insert a guard after line 1:
```
[greet.py#A1B2]
INS.POST 1:
+    if not name: name = "stranger"
```

Replace line 2 with two lines:
```
[greet.py#A1B2]
SWAP 2.=2:
+    greeting = "Hi"
+    msg = f"{greeting}, {name}"
```

Delete line 3:
```
[greet.py#A1B2]
DEL 3
```

Add a header and trailer:
```
[greet.py#A1B2]
INS.HEAD:
+# generated header
INS.TAIL:
+greet("everyone")
```

Insert Markdown bullets — the leading `+` is the body-row marker; the file receives `- task`:
```
[PLAN.md#A1B2]
INS.POST 2:
+- task
+  - nested task
```
</example>

<anti-patterns>
# WRONG — `-` rows / bare context lines do not exist. The range deletes; the body is only the new content.
SWAP 3.=3:
    msg = "Hello, " + name
-   print(msg)
+   return msg
# RIGHT
SWAP 3.=3:
+   return msg

# WRONG — a pure insertion done as a widened `SWAP`: you want to add one line after 2,
# but you replace 2.=4, retype the keepers, and risk dropping one.
SWAP 2.=4:
+    msg = "Hello, " + name
+    extra = compute(name)
+    print(msg)
# RIGHT — touch nothing you keep; the new line is the whole body.
INS.POST 2:
+    extra = compute(name)
</anti-patterns>

<critical>
If you remember nothing else:
1. RE-GROUND AFTER EVERY EDIT. Every apply mints a fresh `#TAG` and renumbers — take the next edit's numbers from the edit response or a fresh hashline `read`. Stale tag or surprise? STOP, re-`read`.
2. RANGES ARE TIGHT. Cover only lines that change; a stale wide range shreds everything it spans.
3. THE BODY IS THE FINAL CONTENT. Every body row starts with `+`; Markdown bullets use `+- item`, not `- item`.
</critical>
